nodes.label: Central law §25.6
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The number of predictions an index can make is E(X); a complete index makes none.

nodes.label: Closed index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: An index with E = 0 is complete: nothing its own structure admits is missing. A complete solution cannot be a trajectory; it must be an index of families.

nodes.label: Cesaro Chain Envelope
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: S_{k+1}<=((k+1)/k)S_k, single-parent at every k; equals R(exact) as sets nine of nine, so the defining system is its own normal form.

nodes.label: Cut Law
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: At a cut on coordinate v a component shrinks iff it holds a parent of v and grows iff a child; 89 tests, one violation at Lambda_9'; earlier 'fails at two-parent coordinates' version withdrawn.

nodes.label: Future as Saturated Bracket
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 0 of 97 (past,present) pairs determine a future; the admissible future set is the full interval of the target lattice; interpolation not extrapolation.

nodes.label: Lambda 9 Prime Falsifier
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The one tower stage whose constraint graph carries a cycle (f-g-2S'-f); the cut law, two-parent uniqueness and the Markov property all fail there, so the theorem is falsifiable and falsified on demand.

nodes.label: Meet-Closure by Concavity
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The exact set is the concave sequences; pointwise minima of concave functions are concave while maxima are not, which is the whole one-sidedness at every n and cap.

nodes.label: n-Body Index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Three-body configuration space indexed and closed (E=0, treewidth 1, four caps) and elevated to n bodies as a chain of Cesaro bounds; nothing here solves the three-body problem.

nodes.label: Past Present Future as a Path
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: past present future as a path
nodes.rationale: The three parts overcount by 1,268 if free but factor exactly conditioned on q; balance holds at every two-sided cut; future is conditionally independent of past given present, a Markov property exact at every value.

nodes.label: q as Articulation Vertex
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Of five cut vertices in the constraint tree, q is the unique one separating source from target; its content as structure is the connection, not the count.

nodes.label: Ravi Substitution
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Masses are tangent lengths of a triangle whose sides are pairwise sums and total mass the semiperimeter; the parity congruence is a real geometric condition.

nodes.label: Second Bridge Pricing
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Twenty (Lambda_8) and sixty-four (Lambda_13) admissible A-side/B-side couplings all preserve closure but most destroy the q-factorisation; exclusivity belongs to the tree, not to closure.

nodes.label: Three Presentations
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Systems A (m1,S,M), B (pairwise sums) and P1 (masses) form a conservation of difficulty: each is free in two of ordering, non-negativity, total-mass cap and pays in the third.

nodes.label: Tick Decomposition
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: k-g = (k-q)+(q-g): retention plus loss in transit, exactly balanced 430 against 430; Pauli is a minority partner (10.3%).

nodes.label: Spanning Tree Identity
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: |E|=|V|-1: to add a bridge and remain a tree one must break an edge or add a coordinate (P16); a second bridge is the three-body problem arriving inside the index.

nodes.label: Treeness Hypothesis
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The decay theorem, Markov property, balance identity and cut law all rest on the constraint graph being a tree; never named as a hypothesis before; 'the tree or the tightness' is where a family of theorems stops applying.

nodes.label: Bounded Lattice Closure
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: All 21,945 pairs of 210 admissible cells close under join and meet; hydrogen (1,0,1) is the unique minimum by theorem, not by choice; greatest element (7,4,18).

nodes.label: Chemical Groups as Fibres
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Fixing (l,k) and varying n gives lines that are conventional chemical groups; seven of eight main groups reproduced exactly.

nodes.label: Helium Placement
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Helium at (1,0,2) falls with the alkaline earths, the Janet placement reached by two independent routes (projection and fibration).

nodes.label: Janet Left-Step Table
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Exactly the projection of the lattice along n+l; a correspondence not an analogy.

nodes.label: Leal Restrepo Ordered Hypergraph
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Orders elements by properties; the present work orders configurations by quantum numbers; complementary, not competing.

nodes.label: Madelung Rule as Linear Functional
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: n+l is a linear functional whose level-set volumes pair 2,2,8,8,18,18,32,32, explaining period-length repetition; Madelung ordering itself remains an empirical input (Kendall tau 0.992, 28 inversions).

nodes.label: Shell Capacity as Lattice Volume
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Counting cells at fixed n returns 2n^2; Pauli capacities are outputs of counting the lattice, not inputs.

nodes.label: Sperner Property
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Must be checked since the lattice is not rank-symmetric; Dilworth via maximum matching gives max antichain 15 = largest rank level.

nodes.label: Young Lattice Coincidence
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 210 = C(10,4) suggests a Young lattice but rank sequences differ and Lambda is unimodal yet not palindromic; recorded so others do not pursue it.

nodes.label: Closure Defect E X
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: E(X)=|R(X)|-|X| counts cells a structure admits and an index denies; the graded measure that distinguishes this framework from literatures that settle membership only.

nodes.label: Closure Operator R
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Extensive, monotone, idempotent; X closed iff X=R(X); Knaster-Tarski guarantees fixed points where a paradox would sit.

nodes.label: Definability versus Reachability
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Lattice order and composition order share only 0.4% of relations; a cell contains its own down-set but reaches only 24.7% of the object; 'nine-dimensional time' is false as dimension and true as the unique dimension at which time exists.

nodes.label: Entry Test
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Reproduce the seven tower cell counts 976/1,654/1,561/2,535/13,585/70,905/199,130 from the book's definitions alone; seven of seven pass, plus twelve further quantities.

nodes.label: Eras as Strongly Connected Components
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Lambda_9's 33 objects fall into three SCCs pure in occupancy (8/15/10), a chain of three; identities sit only at maximal occupancy; survives four cap settings.

nodes.label: Intersection Groupoid
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The 389 cells with g=q=k form a full groupoid, the region where time has no direction, 23.5% of Lambda_9.

nodes.label: Lambda Tower
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Lambda_8 to Lambda_13 at caps (3,3,1,3,1); E(X)=0 at every stage while fill falls 14.12% to 0.42%.

nodes.label: O10 the Destination Coordinate
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Unclosable: naming a destination needs a coordinate the index does not carry; R(X) is inside the product of value sets, so no test can exist.

nodes.label: Reversed Index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Exchanging source and target ends gives a lawful closed index of the same size that is not Lambda_9; reversing time is not a sign change.

nodes.label: Two Recovery Routes
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Every cell of Lambda_8 is restored after deletion (976/976) and every cell of Lambda_9 is a composite of two others; two near-disjoint total routes supply the redundancy the tree denies at coordinate level.

nodes.label: Union Does Not Exist
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Lambda_9 union its reversal has E=2,857 and 830,625 failing pairs; a structure containing both directions of time is unavailable at any price the index recognises.

nodes.label: Paradox and the Negation-Free Language
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The index language has max, min, <= and no negation, so a liar or grandfather loop cannot be written; self-reference becomes an equation solved by the Knaster-Tarski fixed point; paid for with expressive power (no differences, sums or symmetric bounds). Negations are not eliminated but indexed as ordered coordinate values.

nodes.label: Dipole selection rules (Laporte 1924, Russell & Saunders 1925, Wigner 1927)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: dipole selection rules (laporte 1924, russell & saunders 1925, wigner 1927)

nodes.label: The electromagnetic quotient
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Λ₉ modulo the dipole selection rules (|Δℓ|=1, ΔS=0, parity) — a quotient, not a subset. Its E=0 is vacuous (§12.11.8): the image is a complete rectangle, the one closure that certifies nothing. Adjoining multipole and ΔS as coordinates gives E=3; taking the image gives E=0 — quotient versus extension.

nodes.label: The EM crossing (within vs across elements)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: the em crossing (within vs across elements)
nodes.rationale: Within one element EM-allowed transitions compose at 11.6% vs forbidden 40.7%; across the 118 elements the order reverses, 89.7% vs 77.9% — the rule forbidding composition inside an atom enables it between atoms.

nodes.label: Λ_cross — the crossing values
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: a_cross = Δn(√p_g+√p_r)/(p_g−p_r), nineteen surds, E=0 on (Δn, ℓ_g). Ordinal, algebraic (closed in ℚ(√p)) and geometric but not analytic — an integer object that cannot be fitted and needs no fitting.

nodes.label: Λ_descent — the charge dependence
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: a(c) on (c, regime), E=0. The only place a fit belongs; fits applied to the whole of a (crossing plus descent) made constants absorb each other because half the object has no analysis language.

nodes.label: Λ_xray — the inner shell
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Dipole-allowed inner-shell transitions on (Δn, Δℓ, jtype_hole): 33 lines → 9 cells, E=0 (R 1378). Built with no new data — a downward transition was already inside Λ's alphabet, only the caps excluded it. Kα, Lα, Mα are one type at three depths, which Siegbahn notation hides.

nodes.label: The languages — six readings of one index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: the languages — six readings of one index
nodes.rationale: A language is a coordinate system; translation is re-coordinatisation; E is the cost. Order (R), geometry (monotone polyhedron), algebra/logic (Gröbner ideal), analysis (coefficients of F), information (description length), statistics (max-entropy on marginals), and documentary with no operator. Six agree on Λ at 976; all ten pairs hold — a complete graph, not a ladder.

nodes.label: Moseley's law
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Enters Λ_ladder at subvalence as counting/across; analysis speaks of Λ_xray via Moseley at R²=0.998.

nodes.label: NIST SRD 128 / Deslattes et al. 2003, Rev. Mod. Phys. 75

nodes.norm_label: nist srd 128 / deslattes et al. 2003, rev. mod. phys. 75

nodes.label: Integer object
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A quantity with no analysis or statistics language; cells AND values fixed by arithmetic. Λ_cross is the only one; nine of eleven unfixable cells across the work are expectation values and Λ_cross is the exception.

nodes.label: The book's own indexes
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Audits (21 cells, E=16), register (33, E=6), Q (8, E=5), protocols (19, E=105), constraints (15, E=21), mathematics (77, E=0, fibred), numbers, channel survey; book at chapter resolution E=578 vs part resolution E=0. The method self-applied — the only place E>0 is a theorem about shape rather than a collection gap.

nodes.label: Λ_spectra^obs — the channel survey
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Coordinates Z · core charge · ℓ; each cell a Rydberg channel. 596 channels across 313 of 1,664 cells. Unbounded in n so every cap is a decision; three caps (1,664/4,376/55,224) all closed fixed points of R — the unwitnessed count is never a closure defect. Ceiling 98.9% because Sc I and Ti I have no Rydberg series.

nodes.label: Cell grades: MEASURED, BRACKETED, BOUNDED, PROPAGATED, FORMAL, UNCONSTRAINED
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: cell grades: measured, bracketed, bounded, propagated, formal, unconstrained
nodes.rationale: 205/5/42/954/73/33 cells; the grade records how far a statement travelled; 97.5% of the index carries a defensible statement.

nodes.label: Λ_chain — the derived filling index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 119 rows Z=2–120 from the V^{N−1} walk (SCORED 107, UNWITNESSED 12). Closes on itself: each row built from the previous, so 107 of 107 is one score. Carries time — moves Z−1→Z, totally ordered. Supplies from first principles the aufbau ordering Λ cannot supply for itself (Chapter 6); Λ's input column is now a derived object with one constant.

nodes.label: Λ_cinf — the counterfactual twin
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The identical 107-row walk at c→∞; eleven entrants differ and all eleven are wrong against nature. Exists to state that Λ's subject is relativistic; quarantined from every other use (register 1706).

nodes.label: Λ_j120 — the unwitnessed extension
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Twelve rows Z=109–120; cells close, values unwitnessed. Λ's falsification frontier: when a superheavy ground configuration is measured, exactly one row scores or fails (register 1712).

nodes.label: Λ_V5 — the contested-row closure
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Five rows Z=38,56,72,89,105 with the second-order correlation differential over the mean-field margin. Closes by exhaustion; carries no time. Warrant that Λ_chain's mean field carries the exact equation's order: every contested competition widens under correlation (register 1705).

nodes.label: The Löwdin challenge (origin of the n+ℓ rule)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: the lowdin challenge (origin of the n+l rule)
nodes.rationale: Why the n+ℓ ordering holds is unresolved; this work uses the ordering and does not explain it.

nodes.label: The n+ℓ (Madelung) rule
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Janet recognised it in 1928 before Madelung (c.1926, published 1936); shell lengths 2,2,8,8,18,18,32,32 follow by Klechkovski–Hakala.

nodes.label: The Löwdin solution (Chapter 35, registers 1701–1712)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Four transition indexes built beside Λ; closure and time are the questions they exist to answer, so the template differs from Part IX's.

nodes.label: Two-Parent Coordinate g
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: g<=min(q,4f+2), the Pauli coupling, is the unique two-parent bound at all seven tower stages; every higher axis enters with one parent, which is why closure survives thirteen dimensions.

nodes.label: The Method 1.3 The Lach Cylinder
nodes.author: Matthew Lach

nodes.label: A Certificate Has Nothing to Predict
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: a certificate has nothing to predict
nodes.rationale: A ranking function is a certificate supplied by an analyst from a chosen class, so asking what the composition order forecasts asks what a proof technique forecasts; whether any of this is time is the wrong question, which closes O9 rather than deferring it.

nodes.label: Composition as Time
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Reconciles §10.2 (Lambda carries time as before/after) with §F.4.3 (no date may enter Lambda): time is an order between cells, not a stamp on one; premise that time is a single unchanging value during a transition, so the clock ticks only at composition.

nodes.label: Decay Theorem
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: On a tree the coordinates form a Markov random field, mutual information is non-increasing in tree distance by data processing, and Pinsker bounds the overlap of two arrows; decay is proved, the strict ordering only measured.

nodes.label: Markov Random Field on a Tree
nodes.author: Matthew Lach

nodes.label: Time column law §12.11.1.3
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: An index has a time column exactly when its cells are moves; the shape index's cells are configurations, so time is recovered afterwards as a quadrature.

nodes.label: All-or-Nothing by Column
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Of 25 (n,l) columns, 19 are full and 6 empty, none partial; the realised system is one of 120 down-sets of the column poset, at the 79th percentile by size.

nodes.label: Discovery Frontier of Five Addresses
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Maximal occupied cells are Lr (5,3,14), Cn (6,2,10), Og (7,1,6); any new element must occupy one of five covering cells or extend beyond n=7; constrains configuration only, not nuclear stability.

nodes.label: Parity Invariant
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Rank generating function decomposes into shifted q-integers per column and vanishes at q=-1 because every capacity 2(2l+1) is even; the balance (105/105, 59/59) is forced by spin degeneracy.

nodes.label: Periodic System as Order Ideal
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The 118 occupied cells are downward closed without exception; a property of aufbau filling rather than of lattice geometry.

nodes.label: Reserved Cells
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 92 addressed vacancies concentrated at n=6-7 in d,f,g layers, corresponding to beyond Z=118; constrains valence configuration only, says nothing about nuclear stability; earlier 'bounded search' claim withdrawn.

nodes.label: Aufbau as Monotone Accumulation
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Downward closure holds because electrons are added one at a time along a monotone path; lanthanide/actinide irregularities disturb ordering but not closure.

nodes.label: Classification of Empty Space
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Every unoccupied cell is void (l>=n), reactive (k exceeds Pauli capacity) or reserved (valid but unoccupied): 180/240/92 against 118 occupied; gives the table a vocabulary for absence the 2D layout lacks.

nodes.label: Birkhoff Representation Theorem
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The lattice is distributive with 27 join-irreducibles; the periodic system is one element of the lattice of ideals J(Lambda), and discovery is a monotone path upward.

nodes.label: No Cell Is Doubly Irreducible
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 17 join-irreducibles and 17 meet-irreducibles with empty intersection at every cap, so pushback floor and step are one fact.

nodes.label: Pushback
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Pairs of survivors that fail when a cell is removed: floor 16, median 506, U-shaped in rank; weakest where the lattice is widest.

nodes.label: Step Law
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: X minus [a,b] is a sublattice iff a is join-prime and b is meet-prime; minimum removable interval is 4 at book caps; first statement using 'irreducible' refuted by its own test on 35 of 116,138 intervals.

nodes.label: Hydrogenic Labelling Failure
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Unfolding k into (m,s) fails because |m|<=l contains -m<=l with reversed orientation (0 join, 4,040 meet failures); the shift m'=m+l restores closure but destroys the representation-theoretic object, so the four-axis proposal is withdrawn.

nodes.label: Sublattice Intersection Argument
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Closure is inherited, not coincidental: constraints x_i<=f(x_j) with f monotone define sublattices of the box and finite intersections of sublattices are sublattices (Birkhoff 1967).

nodes.label: Order Dimension Three
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Justifies three axes: a standard example S3 among admissible cells forces dim>=3 and the componentwise embedding in N^3 gives <=3; a claim about the order relation, not physical space.

nodes.label: Posetic Coordinates
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Quintero-Bruggemann-Restrepo's up-set/down-set/incomparable triples are visualisation devices, independent of order dimension; applicable to Lambda as a future continuation.

nodes.label: Note on Novelty
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Techniques are textbook; only their application to the configuration lattice is claimed; no thorough literature search performed, so results are offered as correct and checkable, not new.

nodes.label: Membership versus Distance from Membership
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Four times (2-decomposability, interval-dismantling, starshaped class, ranking functions) the literature had the class and not the count; this framework asks how far from membership, which needs a graded quantity the membership question never does.

nodes.label: The parent-term wall
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: An open-shell core gives one interleaved series per parent term converging on different limits; the series are not separable, so no extractable defect. Hence no open-shell ion above charge 6.

nodes.label: Adjacency Result
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Ytterbium (4,3,13) and platinum (5,2,8) are neighbours in the lattice though maximally separated in the printed table; principal structural result of Part I and departure point for Part IV.

nodes.label: Deuteride Host Screen
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Two imported crystallographic filters (hydride-former, FCC) reduce 118 elements to nine; the lattice contributes only the sorting index.

nodes.label: Displacement Vector Delta Q
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Static geometric vector from the excited-pair midpoint back to ground state; carries all element-specific content; invariant under origin translation.

nodes.label: Elemental Lattice
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Treat n, l and k as three independent axes with no new physics; the axes are coupled counts, so distances are combinatorial, which is what allows the classification of empty space. Named for the lattice because the order structure, not the field equation, is the substantive content.

nodes.label: Heuristic Index H cp
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: |Q0| times fractional filling to the power l/4; explicitly a choice, not a derivation; dimensionless sorting device with no interpretation as rate or energy.

nodes.label: Hydride Formation Enthalpy Regression
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Two-term model in l and k gives CV R^2=0.51, outperformed by Pettifor (0.79) and Miedema (0.90); reported as unflattering benchmark rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Kainosymmetry on the Boundary Diagonal
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: First-of-kind subshells 1s,2p,3d,4f,5g are exactly the cells where l=n-1 is tight; locates scattered anomalies at one geometric feature without explaining them.

nodes.label: Occupancy Coordinate k
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The one survivor: k is uncorrelated with every established descriptor and raises Pettifor's CV R^2 from 0.79 to 0.84 (p=0.001); the same coordinate is load-bearing for order closure because its bounds carry no orientation reversal.

nodes.label: Three Geometric Classes
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Classes A/B/C by direction of Delta Q follow from l<=n-1 alone; separates 3d and 4f series (C) from 4d and 5d (B).

nodes.label: Ytterbium Candidate
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: FCC hydride-former, stable, available, apparently untested as a primary deuteride host; a fact about the literature independent of the index.

nodes.label: Convention Dependence of Ordering
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Yb ranks first under two conventions and fourth under a third; a result that depends on the analyst's convention characterises the convention, not the structure, so Table 2 is not a prediction.

nodes.label: Dimensional Obstruction
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Every lattice quantity is a pure number (axes are counts, Lambda in N^3) while Gamow barrier penetration needs kg, J and m; no external scale is supplied, so no falsifiable nuclear prediction exists; scale separation (10^-1 eV/10^-10 m vs 10^5 eV/10^-15 m) means the hydride regression does not soften this.

nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A normalisation construction on the lattice, not a Hamiltonian solution; Omega is formal and the envelope is element-independent, so it is the weakest component of the framework.

nodes.label: The Method — The Lach Cylinder (1.2)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: One claim: a closed index contains its own definition, its own contradiction, and determines what may be added; demonstrated on Λ and reported with every failure (297 withdrawals).

nodes.label: Λ — the atomic index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Eight integer coordinates (n,ℓ,k,q,e,f,g,2S) under eight inequalities, 976 cells, E=0. Its unique contribution is the transfer: cells are moves, not positions, from which composition, time columns and categories follow.

nodes.label: Composable fraction
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Λ₈ composes not at all (four source coordinates vs three target); Λ₁₀ peaks at 80.87% and every later stage falls; non-composable cells at the peak are exactly those with g=0 since k≥1 forbids an empty target being a source.

nodes.label: The eight constraints of Λ
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Hydrogenic ℓ≤n−1, Pauli k≤4ℓ+2, conservation q≤k, target hydrogenic f≤e−1, target Pauli g≤4f+2, g≤q, multiplicity 2S≤k, k≥1; assembled from Bohr/Schrödinger, Stoner, Pauli, Hund — Λ introduces none of them.

nodes.label: Λ_ladder — the ladders themselves
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Fourteen ladders in three families (six species, six state, two X-ray) on (seat, kind, Zcross); nine cells, E=0. A coordinate individuating cells is a KEY, not an axis. Closes once the X-ray pair is seated at subvalence (R 1427); 90% of comparable nine-cell sets refuse so the zero is earned; five shared cells resolve as four findings and one separation (R 1428-1429); tower stage is the discriminator, not an axis.

nodes.label: Λ_t — the corridor position
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Twelve cells on (ℓ,n) holding t=(a−L)/(U−L), E=3 (7p, 6d, 7d). ℓ carries the limit √(ℓ(ℓ+1)/2), n carries the approach; q is not a coordinate.

nodes.label: The space index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The first column: what the index holds. Λ has no spatial coordinate (n, e are shell numbers). The nearest spatial reading is observability: an observer's register is Λ-valued and E(local register) measures what is not yet real to that observer — defined, falsifiable, not yet built.

nodes.label: The time index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Not a coordinate but the second column: what an index can compose. Λ₈ 976/0, Λ₉ 1,654/1,169, Λ₁₀ 2,535/2,050; state indexes cannot have one. A date must never enter Λ — a transition is a type and types are not dated; what Λ lacks is a denominator (claims per session, §12.11.1.1).

nodes.label: The tower Λ₈…Λ₁₃
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Each stage adds one coupling axis (seniority, core J, K, J) and inherits every bound below; E=0 at every stage. Counting axes raise the composable fraction, coupling axes lower it — no exception. Its unique contribution is the measured price of an axis.

nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: the one-line summary — what only each index gives

nodes.label: Charge c is three coordinates in one symbol
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: charge c is three coordinates in one symbol
nodes.rationale: c appears inside u=ln(Nₑ/c^(2/3)), as the base of c^(−x), and in the exponent x; every degeneracy of the session was a charge term trading with something else.

nodes.label: Composition as temporal order
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: §12.11.0: composition IS the temporal order — a cell's source end is a before, its target an after, q is what changed. An index has a time column exactly when its cells are moves.

nodes.label: A coordinate individuating the cells is a key, not an axis
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: a coordinate individuating the cells is a key, not an axis
nodes.rationale: At four ladders fixes was injective by construction so E=0 was forced; at six, ionisation and isotopic both fix Z and the zero becomes earnable — the dual of A.define.

nodes.label: The one coupling g ≤ min(q, 4f+2)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The single non-product term in the generating function is the Pauli principle; removing it takes 976 to 1,000, the 24 excluded cells having f=0, g=3 — three electrons in an s orbital.

nodes.label: Cell as transition (a move, not a state)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: cell as transition (a move, not a state)
nodes.rationale: A cell is a source subshell holding k electrons, q moving, into a target subshell ending with g at spin 2S. Everything in the compendium follows from this.

nodes.label: Λ_amp — the electron–electron term
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Slater integrals F^k, G^k per subshell pair; twenty cells, E=0, a perfect triangle 0≤i≤ℓ. Indexed on multipole rank k gives E=1 (F¹, parity-forbidden); reindexed on position within sequence it closes — the rank is not a free coordinate.

nodes.label: Λ_charge — the roles of the charge
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: λ_charge — the roles of the charge
nodes.rationale: Nine occurrences on (role, carrier, sign, regime), E=0. Declaring the three roles as coordinates in Λ_spectra raises E from 1929 to 13,605: a closed sub-index says nothing about whether the parent wants it.

nodes.label: Λ_chem — the chemical properties
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Forty-two properties on (kind, seat, PCA dependency), E=0 on fourteen cells over subvalence and valence shells; twelve of 42 are properties of bulk matter, not an atom. E climbs 0→3→8→11→19 as core, nucleus, aggregate are added, declaring PCA's domain. Last defect: the ground TERM changes with charge.

nodes.label: Λ_const — the constants
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Fourteen constants on (role, carrier), E=0 at 2 of 576 orderings. Every CENTRE is a small integer or half-integer and no SCALE is.

nodes.label: Λ_law — the laws of the channel equation
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: λ_law — the laws of the channel equation
nodes.rationale: Seven laws on (law, carrier), E=0 at carrier order u<p<ℓ−ℓ_core<Z−T, 288 of 120,960 orderings. Order is monotone in locality; fitting in the wrong carrier took the ℓ-spread from spurious r² 0.868 to real 0.356.

nodes.label: Λ_PCA — physics ⊕ charge ⊕ amplitude
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Nine cells on (source, domain refined by charge regime), E=0. Per-atom calibration: for any (Z,c) it states which parameters apply; low (c=2) closes BEFORE neutral. Earlier merge on axis names raised E 6→11 against a malformed Λ_phys; merged on domain≡regime after the rebuild they close.

nodes.label: Λ_ryd — the Rydberg series
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Five cells on (Ritz order, ℓ, sign), E=0 once δ₂ is INTERMEDIATE. Holds the n-dependence Λ_spectra discards (δ₂, δ₄); the sign of δ₂ is penetration, not ℓ.

nodes.label: Λ_var — the variables
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Twelve variables on (body, role), E=0. No nucleus+rydberg cell: the screening statement as structural fact — the three-body factorisation. Singleton rule: an index is closed when its output class is a singleton.

nodes.label: Λ_phys — the parameter index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Every number taken from physics on four coordinates (kind, source, domain, objects resting on it); 27 parameters, eight this work's own, none universal. Rebuilt on (source, domain) with 21 parameters, E=0: a staircase whose diagonal says a pooled fit across regions asserts a universal parameter the closed index says does not exist. Asks where the work would break first.

nodes.label: Seaton's ratio
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Measured 1.25 where the dipole term gives 1.00; valid at p=0 (1.15±0.21) and undefined at p≥1 — a domain, not a failure.

nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: (Z, charge, ℓ, 2S+1) over 104,832 cells with a defect for each. Unique contribution: values — the only index on which the metric half E_W has anything to measure. Closes at the limit: 98 cells, E=58, 38 needing more electrons than any atom has, eleven of the rest the Madelung exceptions.

nodes.label: Thomas–Fermi exponent
nodes.author: Matthew Lach

nodes.author: Matthew Lach

nodes.author: Matthew Lach

nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 365 cells in a box of 372, E=7 (February's 29-31 and four 31sts). 365=5·73, 73 exceeds every rung so it is genuinely constrained. A subject with no physics: E=7 is the price of keeping January first.

nodes.label: A chessboard — (rank, file)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 64 cells in 64, E=0 because its box IS its cells — the full product with no constraint at all; the ceiling of what E=0 means.

nodes.label: E — the closure defect
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: E(X) is the excess of R(X) over X. E=0 is informative at any density; E>0 at low density measures sparsity only (§1.9). E is coordinate-relative.

nodes.label: R — the closure operator
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: R(X) is every point of the observed box respecting all monotone pairwise envelopes; extensive, monotone, idempotent, closed sets form a Moore family; E(X)=0 exactly when the binary constraint network is globally consistent.

nodes.label: Janet's left-step table — (n+ℓ, Z)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Same 118 elements ordered on n+ℓ; 118 cells in a box of 944, E=0. Demonstrates that E is coordinate-relative on one subject: periodic table vs Janet give E=36 vs E=0.

nodes.label: The nuclide chart — (Z, N)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Measured nuclides by proton and neutron count, E=9; the nine cells are the mass formula's pairing and clustering terms — the only index where E>0 and every missing cell is nameable physics, making the defect a measurement rather than a score.

nodes.label: The periodic table — (period, group)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: 90 cells in a box of 126, E=36 — the 36 are cells the coordinates admit and no element occupies. Its unique role is the control: coordinates fixed by others for other reasons, yet 118 elements and 18,288 constraint tests with zero failures.

nodes.label: Redundancy — how much of an index determines the rest
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: redundancy — how much of an index determines the rest
nodes.rationale: Largest fraction removable with exact recovery under R: Λ 61%, Λ_spectra^obs 20%, others 0%. Coupling does not explain it (r²=0.002, p=0.94; conjecture stated beforehand and wrong); DIMENSION does — projection test on Λ gives 61/30/30/30/5/0% at d=8..3 because R works on d(d−1) pairwise envelopes. Only independent coordinates count: adding Nₑ=Z−c+1 drops redundancy 20%→0%.

nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.norm_label: the two failure modes — order and arity
nodes.rationale: The periodic table is the ordering failure (repairable, re-ordering acts on one relation at a time); the violation index is the arity failure; a vocabulary may also not be indexable at all.
